newsitem.title: USA: Colombia to grow four percent in 1997 - Ocampo.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to grow four percent in 1997 - Ocampo.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said on Tuesday he was confident that Colombia's gross domestic product would grow by around four percent in 1997, up from last year's 2.1 percent increase.
"I think a four percent target, which is really a joint target we have with the Central Bank, is acceptable," he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
Ocampo said the recovery would be fuelled by higher demand, thanks to a decline in domestic interest rates and a rise in coffee prices that started late last year.
Colombia kept interest rates high between late 1994 and early 1996 to cool down its economy and reduce inflation, which had remained hovering stubbornly above 20 percent.
Its economy was also affected by an unexpected drop in the coffee crop between late 1996 and early 1997 and the rising cost of waging war against drug traffickers, Ocampo argued.
Ocampo added that he remained "fairly confident" that Colombian interest rates would continue to decrease.

The central bank's board will meet on May 6 to review its rate policy in the light of April's inflation results. Last week Ocampo, who sits on the board, proposed that the central bank cut its overnight rate by two percentage points to 19.5 percent.
"I'm fairly confident that there will be some reduction in interest rates," he said.
